He argued that Ukrainian strikes in response cause greater damage because Russia’s infrastructure is more centralized. His comments follow attacks on Ukrainian telecommunications facilities and a series of Ukrainian strikes against Yandex data centers.

Putin Lectured Nordic Leaders on History, Zelensky Reveals Kyiv’s Role — Zelensky said Norway and Finland briefed Kyiv before speaking with Putin about a possible November meeting in Abu Dhabi. FT reported that Putin spent much of their 90-minute conversation discussing history, while an immediate ceasefire was barely raised.

Spain High-Speed Train Collision Kills 30 — At least 30 people were killed in a collision between two high-speed trains south of Madrid, with the death toll expected to rise. The crash is Spain’s second major high-speed rail disaster this year, renewing questions about railway safety.

Israel After the Election: Who Will Form a Government? — Israel faces an uncertain political future after an election left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot without a clear majority. Arab parties could prove decisive in forming a government. Commentators see an opportunity for political change, reduced far-right influence and renewed engagement on Gaza, but warn that coalition deadlock could trigger another election in 2027.

Oleshky Truce Holds for 30 Hours as Kherson Falls Quiet — The first 30 hours of the humanitarian ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky passed without incidents, Ukraine’s ombudsman said on Oct. 28. Across the Dnipro in Kherson, residents ventured outdoors and municipal workers reached areas previously difficult to access. The pause is intended to enable aid deliveries and safe civilian departures and is scheduled to last until Nov. 1.

Russian Commander Organized Widescale Fraud Based on Fake ‘Action’ Videos — Russian media reported the case of Lt. Col. Konstantin Frolov on Tuesday, sentenced to 21 years in prison for organizing a breathtaking series of frauds. He and a group of soldiers made fake videos depicting scenes of combat which included self-inflicted wounds to receive medals and financial compensation.

US Proposed Demilitarized Zones in Donbas, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said the US had proposed demilitarized zones in Donbas and on part of the Kinburn Spit during peace negotiations. Ukraine was prepared to discuss a compromise involving a zone on both sides of the front line. The ideas appeared in successive negotiating documents, but no agreement on the territorial issues has been reached.

Zelensky Seeks Managers to Fix Kyiv’s Winter Crisis, but No One Wants to Take the Job — President Volodymyr Zelensky says Kyiv is unprepared for winter and wants experienced managers to help fix the capital’s infrastructure problems. But potential candidates are reluctant to take on the job, as the dispute deepens between Zelensky’s government and Mayor Vitali Klitschko over winter readiness and control of the city.

Zelensky Wants Abu Dhabi Talks Before ‘New Yalta,’ Warns NATO Against Russian Demands — Zelensky wants Ukraine at the table before Washington, Moscow and Beijing discuss the world’s security order. Kyiv is pushing for talks with the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi, while warning that Putin could use renewed peace negotiations to extract concessions on NATO’s military presence in Europe. Zelensky Warns of Russia’s ‘Economic Marriage’ With US as Ukraine Feels ‘Home Alone’ Without Patriots — Zelensky warned that Russia could use energy and economic deals to draw the US into an arrangement with hidden long-term costs. He also highlighted Ukraine’s shortage of Patriot missiles, disputes over security guarantees, and the resumption of US-Ukraine intelligence sharing.

Safeguards Against ‘Trojan Horses’ in EU Will ‘Bite Hard,’ Warns Enlargement Chief — EU Enlargement Commissioner said Serbia’s EU accession prospects depend on progress in democracy, the rule of law and anti-corruption, as well as alignment with EU foreign policy, particularly regarding Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Israel’s Elections: What Happens Next? — With Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition each projected to win around 51 seats, neither has a clear path to a majority. Coalition talks, a minority government, a unity deal or another election are the four possible outcomes.

Ukraine Strikes Russia’s Largest Steel Plant, Chemical Factory Amid 531 Drone Claims — Fires were reported at Russia’s Novolipetsk Steel Plant and the Azot chemical plant in the Tula region following overnight attacks on Oct. 28. Moscow claimed its air defenses intercepted and destroyed 531 Ukrainian drones, while Kyiv has not commented on its involvement.

Trump Says Putin-Zelensky Meeting Will Be Arranged ‘Very Soon,’ Claims Progress on Ukraine Peace — US President Donald Trump said a meeting between President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin would be arranged “very soon,” claiming that Washington was making significant progress toward ending the war. The announcement came six days before the Nov. 3 US midterm elections, with trilateral peace talks expected in November.

Putin and Pezeshkian Honor Khamenei, Killed in US-Israeli Strikes, and Challenge US Influence — Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told Vladimir Putin that Middle Eastern countries could resolve regional conflicts without US involvement, calling for stronger ties with Moscow. Both leaders paid tribute to Iran’s late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, while discussing military cooperation, energy projects and growing trade. Zelensky: Europe Must Be Included in November Peace Talks — President Volodymyr Zelensky insisted that European countries must participate in upcoming US-mediated peace negotiations with Russia, warning that no European partner should be excluded. His remarks followed a rare phone call between Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Vladimir Putin, ahead of expected trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi in November.

Zelensky Urges US to End Month-Long Patriot Missile Delay as Russian Strikes Kill Civilians — President Volodymyr Zelensky urged Washington to authorize Patriot and NASAMS missile deliveries delayed for nearly a month, warning that interceptor shortages are leaving Ukrainian civilians vulnerable to deadly Russian ballistic attacks. His appeal followed strikes on Kyiv that damaged a university campus, student dormitories and critical infrastructure.

Russian Strike Hits Kharkiv Apartment Building, Injures 5 Including 4-Year-Old Boy — A Russian attack on Kharkiv’s Osnovianskyi district late on Oct. 27 hit a residential apartment building, injuring five people, including a four-year-old boy. Local officials reported that people were trapped inside as emergency crews responded.

Israel Election: Four Scenarios as Opposition Edges Netanyahu but Falls Short of Majority — Israel faces uncertain coalition talks after exit polls projected 52–53 seats for Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc and 50 for Benjamin Netanyahu’s allies. Arab Israeli parties could become kingmakers, while a minority government, national unity coalition or fresh elections remain possible.

Trump Administration Weighs Lifting Sanctions on Kremlin’s Investment Fund – NYT — The New York Times reported that the Trump administration is reviewing a request to lift sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund, led by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev. Ukraine Recaptures Territory, Forces on the Offensive, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky ranked Veles, an underground operation conducted by the National Guard’s Khartiia Corps near Kupiansk, among Ukraine’s three landmark operations this year. According to him, Ukraine’s frontline positions are currently the strongest they have been in a long time, noting that stronger air-defense support would bolster the country’s diplomatic position.

Poland to Host €227M Patriot Missile Service Center — Poland has been selected to host Europe’s service center for PAC-3 interceptor missiles used in the US-made Patriot air defense system, beating Germany, the Netherlands and Norway. The hub aims to cut repair times for interceptors that are already in short supply worldwide and critical to Ukraine’s defense.

‘Trump Is Cooked’: How Trump’s Russia Policy Is Splintering Republicans Ahead of the Midterms — In this video, we break down the shifting MAGA momentum, the political fallout of the Russia-Ukraine policy pivot, what it all means for the upcoming midterms.

Ukraine Moves Closer to Its Own Satellite Network as Test Craft Reaches Orbit — Ukrainian company Himera and Danish firm GomSpace have sent Obria Nano, a test satellite, into orbit as the first step toward an independent Ukrainian communications network. The launch comes as Kyiv seeks to reduce its dependence on SpaceX’s Starshield service amid recent disruptions and strained ties with Washington.

POW Dispute: South Korea Pulls 8 Diplomats From Ukraine — South Korea has withdrawn eight diplomatic personnel from Ukraine amid a dispute over Kyiv’s disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war. Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said talks with his Ukrainian counterpart were continuing, while essential embassy personnel remained in the country and Seoul’s broader support for Ukraine was unchanged.

Kyiv Plans $22 Million in New Water Crossings Over Dnipro River — Kyiv plans to spend Hr.1 billion ($22 million) on new water crossings over the Dnipro River and access roads, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The announcement comes after a Russian ballistic missile attack damaged the South Bridge and metro infrastructure overnight on Oct. 27.

UN Says Russia’s Energy Attacks Possibly Crimes Against Humanity — A UN report published on Oct. 19 says Russia’s attacks on Ukraine’s energy grid show clear intent to deprive the civilian population of life’s necessities and may amount to crimes against humanity. Kyiv has warned of Russia’s plans to disable 90% of the country’s utility services, with the energy grid already strained from over four years of full-scale Russian invasion.

Putin-Linked Boxing Chief Seen Hunting With Trump Jr. in Mongolia — Putin-linked boxing chief Umar Kremlev hunted with Donald Trump Jr. in Mongolia after reportedly funding the US president’s son’s wedding, the Financial Times reported. The trips have raised questions about the relationship between Trump Jr. and a businessman with close ties to the Kremlin.

Rada Extends Residency Deadline for Foreign Soldiers — Ukraine’s Verkhovna Rada approved legislation extending the transitional period for foreign and stateless service members to apply for temporary residence permits from six months to one year. The bill also provides a separate three-month window after signing a military contract and addresses legal status after discharge. Adopted Oct. 27, the legislation was being prepared for signing.

Ukraine Develops Ground Robots That Launch Interceptor Drones — Ukraine’s Ratel Robotics is developing interceptor drones launched from unmanned ground vehicles, starting with multi-rotor models before moving to fixed-wing designs. The company has invested about $200,000 in its aerial division, while fixed-wing development could cost millions.

Oleshky Ceasefire to Last Until Nov. 1, Arakhamia Says — A humanitarian ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky is scheduled to last until late on Nov. 1, Ukrainian lawmaker David Arakhamia said. The pause is intended to enable aid deliveries and civilian evacuations, while Ukraine’s ombudsman reported that both sides were observing the agreement after it took effect early Tuesday.

Germany’s Helsing Unveils Low-Cost Highspeed Drone Interceptors — On Monday Helsing the German defense technology and artificial intelligence company announced the Contra AI enhanced air defense system alongside two highspeed missile interceptors. It is intended to run down Russia’s jet-powered drones and cruise missiles.

Russia Says Three Tankers With Diesel En Route to US — Three tankers carrying Russian diesel are heading to the US under a deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin to ease sanctions, prompting backlash from Kyiv and European allies. A fourth tanker is expected to depart Wednesday, as the agreement strains US-Ukraine relations ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Kremlin Reiterates Moscow Invitation to Zelensky After ‘Frank’ Discussion With Finnish, Norwegian Leaders — Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to end his country’s  war against Ukraine and resume negotiations. During a joint phone call, the leaders reaffirmed their support for Kyiv and stressed that the conflict’s outcome directly affects their countries and wider European security. Will Trump Nominate Orbán as UN Secretary-General? — A Wall Street Journal report suggesting the Trump administration may back Viktor Orbán for UN Secretary-General has sparked debate in Hungary. Political scientist Gábor Török says the potential candidacy could reshape Hungarian politics, while foreign policy expert István Szent-Iványi highlights the irony of Orbán pursuing a role he once criticized as a refuge for failed politicians.

Russian Commander Complains NATO Testing Drones on Ukraine’s Front Line — The commander of Russia’s Akhmat special forces unit told TASS that drones manufactured in NATO countries were being tested against Moscow’s troops. A claim Ukraine’s Defense Ministry partially confirmed in July.

‘Delays Directly Assist Russia’: Zelensky Slams Slow Delivery of Interceptors — Zelensky said prolonged delays in Patriot and NASAMS interceptor deliveries are helping Russia sustain its attacks after an overnight assault involving 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones. At least 15 people were injured in a strike on a Kyiv university campus and surrounding area.

Kremlin Woos Trump’s Circle With Business Deals – Le Monde — Russia is pitching economic cooperation to Donald Trump and his associates without first ending its war against Ukraine, according to Le Monde. A US proposal to restore Russian energy supplies to Europe through Ukraine reportedly alarmed Kyiv because it resembled ideas promoted by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev.
Remembering Adnan Kivan: a Legacy With a Future — A personal tribute to the late owner of Kyiv Post, who transformed the publication into Ukraine’s genuine “global voice.”

Nord Stream Trial Continues as Court Rejects Defence Bid to Halt Proceedings — German prosecutors urged a Hamburg court to reject a defense request to halt the Nord Stream sabotage trial, arguing that Ukrainian military secrecy obligations do not prevent Serhii Kuznetsov from receiving a fair trial. The court had not announced a decision as of publication.

What Israel’s Election Could Change for Ukraine and Relations With Russia — Israelis head to the polls focused on security, living costs, and domestic divisions. Opposition leader Yair Lapid has promised greater support for Ukraine, while Netanyahu’s government has pursued a cautious rapprochement. For Kyiv, the test will be whether those positions produce practical military cooperation.

Russia Observing Ceasefire in Occupied Oleshky as Humanitarian Mission Begins — Russian forces were observing a localized ceasefire around occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast as of 9 a.m. on Oct. 27, Ukraine’s Marine Corps said, as a humanitarian mission began in the city amid worsening conditions for civilians.

Moscow to Restrict Mobile Internet for 3 Days During Putin’s Summits — Moscow will restrict mobile internet for three days during the Gas Exporting Countries Forum and Russia-Africa summit, citing security concerns. The shutdowns come amid intensified Ukrainian drone attacks on the Moscow region and follow weeks-long outages in the capital earlier this year.

Ukraine Downs 2 Ballistic Missiles, 255 Russian Drones in Overnight Attack Targeting Kyiv — Ukrainian air defenses shot down or neutralized two ballistic missiles and 255 Russian drones during an overnight attack primarily targeting Kyiv, the Air Force reported. Impacts were recorded at 25 locations.

Israel to Give Verdict on Netanyahu in Pivotal Election — Israelis are voting in a closely contested election that could end Netanyahu’s long rule after the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack. Security, accountability for the failures, and Israel’s rightward shift dominate the race, with coalition talks likely to take weeks or months.

Ukraine Asks 5 European Allies for Patriot Missiles — Ukraine has asked the UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Poland to provide 10% of their existing Patriot and IRIS-T interceptor stocks in exchange for future deliveries. He also discussed restored US intelligence sharing and Starlink capabilities.

Russian Strike Damages Kyiv’s South Bridge, Traffic Disrupted — Russian attacks overnight into Tuesday, Oct. 27 prompted restrictions on Kyiv’s South Bridge and disrupted the Green Line metro. Mayor released the first photos of the damage as specialists assess the crossing, with no reopening time announced.

Ukraine Confirms Honoring US-Brokered Truce in Russian-Occupied Oleshky — Ukrainian Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets confirmed that the US-brokered ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky took effect Tuesday and that Ukraine is honoring its commitments. The agreement aims to facilitate humanitarian aid and evacuations, but implementation and monitoring arrangements remain unclear.

Ukraine has threatened to boycott the event and challenge the decision through diplomatic and legal channels.

Russian Missiles Strike Kyiv University Campus – 1 Killed, 15 Wounded, Mostly Students — Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv’s university district, killing one person and injuring over 10, mostly students. Zelensky warned of further attacks and urged allies to accelerate air defense deliveries.

Ukraine, Moldova Sign New Military Cooperation Agreement, Vow to Join EU Together — President Volodymyr Zelensky and Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi met with Prime Minister of Moldova Vasily Tofan on Monday, Oct. 26, aimed at broadening cooperation and deepening bilateral ties. The company reported damage in Dubno, Kharkiv, Kovel, Kyiv, Pervomaisk, Poltava, Uman, Vinnytsia and Zaporizhzhia.

Third Political Prisoner Dies in Russia This Month – Report — Aleksandr Kondratov, a 52-year-old production designer charged with treason in Russia, has died in a Moscow hospital after being transferred from pretrial detention, a rights group said. Rights group First Department counted his death as at least the 11th this year among individuals prosecuted in politically motivated cases. The cause of his death has not been disclosed.

Ukraine Extends Martial Law and Mobilization Until Jan. 29 — President Volodymyr Zelensky has signed documents on extending martial law and general mobilization in Ukraine by 90 days, until Jan. 29, 2027, the same day parliament approved them. Ukraine has renewed both measures every three months since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022. Separately on Monday, Oct. 26, Zelensky also enacted a decree on city defenses.

12-Year-Old Boy Dies After Weeklong Fight for Life Following Russian Strike on Nova Vodolaha Park — Twelve-year-old Artem Koval died in a Kyiv hospital on Monday, Oct. 26, after a week of fighting for his life following a Russian drone attack on a crowded park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv region. The strike killed his eight-year-old sister Arina and five other civilians, including an infant, who was just over a year old when she was killed sitting in her stroller.

Russia has used the occupied city as a key defensive position for more than four years. How is this initiative viewed in Ukraine?

Ukraine Plans Draft Reform to End Street Conscription — Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi wants a new mobilization arrangement agreed to with businesses by Dec. 1, aiming to replace street conscription with more predictable enlistment. The proposed model would link full workforce deferments to voluntary military service by some employees and help make troop rotations possible. Detailed terms, including service duration and employer obligations, remain under development.

‘Nearly a Month’: Zelensky Presses US Over Delayed Missile Deliveries — On Monday, Zelensky said Ukraine would again raise delayed US deliveries of Patriot and NASAMS missiles, awaiting Hegseth’s signature for nearly a month. Kyiv is also seeking interceptors from European partners, replenishing energy equipment reserves, and pushing to accelerate November’s Ramstein commitments.

EU Mission Discuss Oversight of Ukraine Support Loan Funds — Ukraine’s Defense Ministry discussed verification and control of money from the EU’s Ukraine Support Loan with a joint European Commission and EU diplomatic service mission visiting the country. The ministry said it presented its 2027 defense funding needs, with a focus on drones and long-range weapons. The loan provides up to €90 billion for 2026-2027.

Elections in Israel: Can Netanyahu Hold on to Power? — Israel’s upcoming parliamentary election pits Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing religious bloc against a more moderate opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot. Key issues include security, accountability for the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack, Haredi military conscription and inflation. Vučić’s Defeat Is Not Yet a Victory for Serbia’s European Future — The victory in Serbia of the Student List raises many questions for the country’s future and its relationship with Ukraine. Among them: Will ministers have the political backing to continue cooperating with Kyiv when the nationalist wing of their alliance objects?

Kremlin Urges Serbia’s New Leaders to Maintain Russia Ties After Vucic’s Election Defeat — The Kremlin urged Serbia’s incoming leaders to maintain ties with Russia after a student-backed opposition movement defeated longtime Moscow-friendly leader Aleksandar Vucic in parliamentary elections. Vucic predicted the new authorities would impose sanctions on Moscow, but the winners had pledged to oppose them.

Ukraine Seeks Earlier Russia Talks and EU Role — Ukraine and the United States are trying to bring planned talks with Russia forward by at least a week, Ukrainska Pravda reported. Kyiv also wants European representatives involved, potentially through briefings alongside the negotiations. Moscow had not confirmed an earlier date as of the evening of Oct. 25, and Ukrainian officials expect several rounds before concrete agreements emerge.

Serbia’s Vucic Loses Vote, Predicts Sanctions on Russia — Serbia’s former president Aleksandar Vucic conceded his coalition’s defeat in Sunday’s parliamentary election and predicted that the next government would impose sanctions on Russia by March or April. The student-backed opposition was projected to secure a majority in the 250-seat assembly. Its pre-election platform, however, pledged to maintain Serbia’s opposition to sanctions against Moscow.

‘Enough for Years’: Ihnat Says Patriot Missiles Used in Middle East Could Have Protected Ukraine — Ukraine could have sustained its Patriot air defense systems for several more years with the missiles expended in the Middle East, Air Force official Ihnat said. He attributed Ukraine’s more efficient use of interceptors to combat experience and flexible tactics.

Trump to Nominate Viktor Orbán as UN Secretary General — WSJ reported on Sunday that the US administration have invited former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán to enter the race for the next UN Secretary-General. Its sources suggested Orbán would secure eight or 10 UN Security Council votes “without much difficulty.”

‘Historic Victory’: World Leaders Celebrate Lula’s Re-Election — Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won re-election with 51.8% of the vote, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro despite his refusal to concede. Leaders across Europe, Latin America and beyond congratulated Lula, hailing the result as a victory for democracy and a boost for progressive politics amid a regional shift to the right.

Russia May Seek NATO Rollback to 1997 in Ukraine Talks — Russia may use renewed peace talks on Ukraine to press for concessions on NATO’s expansion and military presence in Europe, The Telegraph reported on Sunday, citing diplomatic sources. The Kremlin could seek a return to NATO’s 1997 configuration, which would potentially require the withdrawal of allied forces from Poland, the Baltic states, and Finland. No such demand has been publicly confirmed as part of the talks’ agenda.

Former Russian President Calls on Trump to ‘Remove’ Zelensky — Dmitry Medvedev posted a call to US President Donald Trump to use the CIA and the military to “get rid of” Volodymyr Zelensky on MaxMessenger on Sunday. His post justified his demands with a mix of unproven grievances and accusations against Ukraine’s president.

Russia Says Ukraine Peace Talks Won’t Slow War, Open to Local Truces — Russia says upcoming US-brokered peace talks will not slow its war against Ukraine but signals openness to local humanitarian truces. The Kremlin’s stance comes as a ceasefire is planned for Russian-occupied Oleshky to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations.

Pentagon Prepares US Military Bases to Operate Independently for 90 Days in Major War — The Pentagon is preparing US military bases to operate independently for at least 90 days during a major war, with plans for backup power, fuel, andwater supplies, weapons stockpiles, and alternative supply chains to keep US forces running if critical infrastructure fails.

It’s About Security, Stupid! — Whether it is called peace, a ceasefire, or simply an end to the killing, Ukraine’s overriding concern after more than four years of full-scale war is security. Everything else matters only insofar as it strengthens or undermines the country’s ability to defend itself.

Bulgarian Presidential Election Exposes Split Over Ukraine War — Bulgaria’s pro-Russia President Iliana Iotova narrowly led the first round of elections but fell short of expectations, setting up a Nov. 1 runoff against pro-Western challenger Andrey Gyurov amid tensions over suspected drone attacks in the Black Sea.

Zelensky Says Ukraine Wants to Keep 800,000-Troop Army, Rules Out Neutrality — Zelensky said Ukraine wants to maintain an 800,000-strong army unless NATO membership changes its security needs, and ruled out neutrality or restrictions on its forces. He also outlined possible steps toward peace, including an energy truce, prisoner exchange and humanitarian mission in Oleshky.

Russia Won’t Negotiate Seriously While It Thinks It Can Force Ukraine to Surrender, Sybiha Says — Ukraine’s foreign minister says Russia will not negotiate seriously while it believes it can force Kyiv to surrender. His remarks come as Moscow signals readiness to resume trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US in November.

Zelensky: Ukraine Offered US 3 Ways to Stop Strikes on Russian Oil Refineries — Zelensky said Ukraine was prepared to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries if Russia stopped attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure, the US enabled Starlink coverage over Russia, or Washington supplied Patriot missiles. He also warned against lifting sanctions before peace negotiations, saying Ukraine must retain leverage over Moscow.

Voronezh Business Center Hit in Drone Attack as 20 Rail Cars Derail Elsewhere in Russia — A reported drone attack damaged a business center and residential buildings in Voronezh, while industrial and aviation facilities may also have been targeted. Separately, a train derailment in Sverdlovsk Region left seven fuel tankers burning.

Serbia’s Student Movement Ousts Longtime Leader in Parliament Poll — Serbia’s student-led movement declared victory in snap parliamentary elections, ending 14 years of rule by Vucic’s party. The movement’s rise followed nearly two years of anti-government protests over corruption linked to a 2024 railway station disaster that killed 16 people.
